Note that $\Th{PA} \Proves \lforall[x][\lforall[y][(x < y \lif (x' < y
    \lor x' = y))]]$. Thus, if $u 
sless v$, we also have $u 
splus
n^
ssucc 
sless v$ for any~$n$ if $[u] 
eq [v]$.

Any $u \in [x]$ is $
sless y$: $x 
sless y$ by assumption. If $u

sless x$, $u 
sless y$ by transitivity. And if $x 
sless u$ but $u
\in [x]$, we have $u = x
splus n^
ssucc$ for some~$n$, and so $u

sless y$ by the fact just proved.
  
Now suppose that $v \in [y]$ is $
sless y$, i.e., $v 
splus
m^
ssucc = y$ for some standard~$m$. This rules out $v 
sless x$,
otherwise $y = v 
splus m^
ssucc 
sless x$. Clearly also, $x 
eq
v$, otherwise $x 
splus m^
ssucc = v 
splus m^
ssucc = y$ and we
would have $[x] = [y]$. So, $x 
sless v$. But then also $x 
splus
n^
ssucc 
sless v$ for any~$n$. Hence, if $x 
sless u$ and $u \in
[x]$, we have $u 
sless v$. If $u 
sless x$ then $u 
sless v$ by
transitivity.

Lastly, if $y 
sless v$, $u 
sless v$ since, as we've shown, $u

sless y$ and $y 
sless v$.
